title: Natural Domain of a Dual Radicand Inequality System
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain of the function f(x) = \sqrt{\frac{x - 1}{x + 3}} + \sqrt{\frac{4 - x}{x + 1}} by solving the simultaneous system of rational inequalities and determining their intersection.
hints: The sum of two functions is defined if and only if the input lies in the intersection of their individual domains: dom(f) = dom(f_1) intersect dom(f_2).
For the first radical, solve (x - 1)/(x + 3) >= 0 with x != -3 using a sign chart.
For the second radical, solve (4 - x)/(x + 1) >= 0 with x != -1 using a sign chart.
Find the set intersection of the two solution sets on the real number line.

steps.title: State the Simultaneous Domain Conditions
steps.explanation: Both square roots must simultaneously evaluate to non-negative real numbers, and neither denominator may equal zero.
steps.why: The domain of a sum of functions is the intersection of their individual domains.

steps.title: Solve the First Rational Inequality
steps.explanation: Critical numbers are x = -3 (denominator singularity) and x = 1 (numerator zero). Testing signs: for x < -3, (-)/(-) = +; for -3 < x < 1, (-)/(+) = -; for x > 1, (+)/(+) = +. Including the valid root x = 1 gives D_1 = (-inf, -3) U [1, inf).
steps.why: Rational inequalities change sign only at real roots of the numerator and denominator.

steps.title: Solve the Second Rational Inequality
steps.explanation: Critical numbers are x = -1 (denominator singularity) and x = 4 (numerator zero). Testing signs: for x < -1, (+)/(-) = -; for -1 < x < 4, (+)/(+) = +; for x > 4, (-)/(+) = -. Including the valid root x = 4 and excluding x = -1 gives D_2 = (-1, 4].
steps.why: Excluding denominator zeros prevents division by zero while preserving valid numerator roots.

steps.title: Compute the Set Intersection
steps.explanation: The interval (-1, 4] has no overlap with (-inf, -3) because -1 > -3. The overlap between (-1, 4] and [1, inf) is precisely the closed interval [1, 4].
steps.why: An input must satisfy all component conditions simultaneously to belong to the domain of the combined function.
